_readme: The story of a run, told over the uplink. tools/gen_voice.py reads this file and renders audio/voice/<id>.wav for every entry with a voice; scripts/comms.gd reads it at load. Keep lines short - they are printed on a 3D console screen and spoken at the same time.

text: Kestrel-9, Gateway. Morning, Vasquez.
Board is green down here. Relief shuttle is
still booked for day eight, so it is you and
the deck for one more week.
Send us your shift report when you close out.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. Shift report follows.
Maintenance complete. Deck is quiet.
Solo crew, one of one. Nothing to log.
Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Report received, thank you.
Flight has a question on your power trace.
Deck lighting drew current for nine minutes
at zero three hundred station time. You were
asleep. Log what you find. No rush on it.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. Shift report follows.
Tasks closed. Checked the lighting bus.
No fault, no log entry, breakers cold.
Something switched them on. Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Copy your lighting note.
Life support is scrubbing carbon dioxide for
two people. It has been for six days.
We are not saying anything by that.
Confirm your crew count on the next pass.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. Crew count is one.
One of one. I walked the whole deck to say it.
Scrubber is running hot, I swapped the filter.
Ask flight what else breathes. Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Understood, one of one.
And no, we do not know what else breathes.
Vasquez, we are answering a report you have
not sent yet. Round trip to you is four
minutes. Check your clock against ours.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. My clock says what yours
says. Your answer landed before I keyed up.
I am reading the words back off my own screen.
Tasks are closed. I would like the shuttle early.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Stop transmitting at night.
We logged eleven minutes of carrier from your
airlock at zero two forty. Voice traffic.
We ran it against your file, Vasquez.
It is your voice. It is asking to be let in.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. I was in my pod at zero
two forty. The airlock panel was dark.
Do not answer it. Whatever keys that mic,
do not answer it. Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Relief shuttle is away,
docking in your day eight. Good news.
On the hail, your station answered ours
with a crew manifest. It reported two souls
aboard. Vasquez, confirm that you are alone.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. I am alone.
I am alone and I am not the one
sending you a manifest.
Tell the shuttle to come in lit. Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Last night, then home.
Shuttle is on approach. Listen to this part.
Do not open the inner hatch until they have
hard dock and they say your name.
Whatever answers before that, do not open it.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. Copy, hatch stays shut.
Last shift is closed out. Deck is secure.
I will be at the window with the light on.
One of one. Vasquez out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Morning, Vasquez.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. Morning, Vasquez.
Crew count is one. One of one.
I walked the whole deck to say it.
Gateway, Kestrel-9. Manifest follows.
Two souls aboard. Two of two.
One is in the power plant with a light.
One is behind him. Kestrel-9 out.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. We did not get a report
off you last shift. The uplink says you were
at the console. Key up and talk to us.
Somebody has to know you are still there.
Kestrel-9, Gateway. We have hard dock.
They have your hatch. They are saying your
name, Vasquez. Open it and come home.
Gateway out. It was good working with you.
